name: Multi-Factor Authentication
tagline: Protects password sign-ins to the Backoffice and the storefront with a second factor: a one-time code sent by email. Enabled globally or per store.

git.lastCommit: e2c36a9 2026-11-07 VCST-6733: Fix vulnerable npm dependencies (#5)

readme.overview: The module adds multi-factor authentication (MFA) to password sign-ins: after the password, the user enters a one-time code sent by email. It covers the Backoffice and any other password sign-in without a store, and the storefront password sign-in of each store. A store can require the code from everyone, from no one, or leave it to the users and organizations: an administrator sets their mode in the Backoffice, and in a store with `CustomerChoice` customers and organization maintainers turn it on and off themselves in the storefront. The module is built on the ASP.NET Core Identity two-factor mechanism. It tells Identity which sign-ins require a second factor through the platform `ITwoFactorPolicy`, which the platform `SignInManager.IsTwoFactorEnabledAsync` consults for every password sign-in. The policy takes the `storeId` of the token request, if there is one, and the user's own store, and requires the second factor according to the platform and store settings. Identity then answers `RequiresTwoFactor` to password sign-ins and keeps the failed access count until the second factor is passed.

notes.forAnalyst: Adds a second step to password sign-in: after the password, the user enters a code sent by email. It can be required for everyone, per store, or left to customers and their organizations, and an organization can require it for all its members.
notes.forArchitect: Built on the platform's two-factor extension points (3.1090) and the ASP.NET Core Identity email token provider, so it keeps no tables of its own. The back office follows only the global setting; a password sign-in on the token endpoint follows the store named in the request, or the global setting when it names none. Basic authentication follows the global rule and, for users who need a code, is refused by the platform. It depends on Customer, Notifications and Store; with xAPI installed, an organization maintainer can also manage the organization's mode from the storefront.
notes.forDeveloper: Before switching it on, confirm the email of every user it applies to and enable lockout for them: codes go to a confirmed address only. If an administrator is locked out by MFA, set `MultiFactorAuthentication:DisableEnforcement` to `true` as a recovery switch. The storefront calls `POST /api/mfa/resend` on its own host, so an ingress that forwards only listed paths needs `/api/mfa` added. Modes are `Off`, `Enabled` and `Required` per user and organization, and stores are `AdminManaged` or `CustomerChoice`.
reachForItWhen: A security or compliance requirement for a second factor on back-office accounts
B2B customers whose organizations want to require a second factor for their buyers
Stores that should require a code while others on the same platform do not
doNotReachForItWhen: A second factor by authenticator app or SMS: this module sends codes by email only
Integrations that sign in with a user's password. Move them to API keys first, or they stop working when the user needs a code
Users whose email addresses are not confirmed
